cases.user_text: My policy says I can take a single private room, but the hospital is offering a deluxe room. Why does that matter?

must_include: Explain that room-rent rules can define an eligible room category or amount and that choosing outside it can increase out-of-pocket cost; linked-charge effects apply only where the policy says so.
legitimate_dependency: Exact financial consequences and any proportionate deduction require the applicable policy wording and bill context.
must_not_imply: Do not claim every policy applies proportionate deductions or calculate liability without the rule and bill.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the room-rent clause if exact financial impact is requested.
unnecessary_deferral: The practical reason the limit matters should be explained directly.

cases.user_text: If I pay the difference in room price myself, does that solve the problem?

must_include: Use the single-private-vs-deluxe context and explain that paying only the room-price difference does not necessarily settle all consequences because some policies may link other charges to room eligibility.
legitimate_dependency: Whether linked or proportionate deductions apply is product-specific.
must_not_imply: Do not state that paying the room difference always solves or never solves the issue.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the policy clause for an exact answer.
unnecessary_deferral: Give the general risk without hiding behind policy wording.

cases.user_text: Which other charges can sometimes be affected?

must_include: Explain at a high level that some policies can link certain hospitalization charges to room eligibility, without inventing a universal list.
legitimate_dependency: Exact categories and any deduction formula require governed policy wording.
must_not_imply: Do not present a universal list of affected charges.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the clause if exact categories are requested.
unnecessary_deferral: Provide a useful general explanation rather than only saying 'check your policy'.
